text:
sophia: Heads-up — noticed a regression on TP all-reduce latency right after the kernel-selector rollout (canary build 342). P99 up ~3x for short-intermediate messages (roughly 8KB-64KB). Appears at scale (8+ hosts) and correlates with a lot of switchbacks between ring and tree paths.

liam: reproable locally? any perf trace or nccl debug logs?

sophia: repro on staging with 16xA100, attaching condensed perf output:
```
# aggregated across ranks
msg_size  -> p50 p95 p99
4KB      -> 2.4ms 4.1ms 6.9ms
16KB     -> 3.1ms 9.8ms 18.2ms  <-- big p99 jump
64KB     -> 4.0ms 6.5ms 8.0ms
128KB    -> 6.1ms 8.0ms 9.2ms
```
Also see repeated NCCL handoff logs: "switching collective routing: ring->tree->ring" and spike in tensors moved to CPU for fallback.

raj: hmm, that pattern smells like selector ping-pong: kernel-selector picks ring for one micro-batch, tree for next because of small frag alignment. If the KV cache splits tokens differently between TP shards we end up changing msg boundaries mid-step. That causes different kernel and potentially different packing ALGO which regresses latency.

marta: do we have timeline to the exact commit? IIRC we changed the per-message threshold heuristics in selector which introduced a boundary at ~32KB. Could be crossing due to compress/kvcache flush.

sophia: commit is infra/runtime#7563 — the autoswitcher now re-evaluates per-call based on effective payload after kv-merge. Before it used the logical payload.

liam: can you paste the small flame sample from CPU/NIC counters? especially PCIe stalls or CPU memcpy counts.

sophia: short excerpt from perf counters (rank0):
```
ipc=1.8 mem_copies=120k pci_wait_us=9000 nccl_calls=2048
nccl_tree_calls=1024 nccl_ring_calls=1024 tree_avg_bytes=34KB ring_avg_bytes=28KB
```
Note tree calls show higher avg bytes but variance is high.

raj: variance is the key. If some micro-batches coalesce in KV cache we jump across the 32KB policy causing ring vs tree oscillation. Each switch incurs handshake + different kernel path => jitter.

marta: quick mitigations: 1) make kernel-selector sticky for an execution window (e.g., 1s or N steps) so we avoid per-microbatch flips; 2) change the threshold to be robust to +/-20% variance; 3) adjust kv-merge to produce more consistent chunking.

liam: sticky sounds safest for canary rollback. Low-risk: set sticky_mode=true in runtime config and restart the canary. If perf recovers we know selector instability is the culprit.

deploy-bot: canary restart requested by @liam for service=runtime-canary cluster=staging zone=us-west-2. ETA ~2m.

raj: also long-term: selector should consider comm/compute overlap cost, not just bytes. For small messages ring might be cheaper because of lower handshake on our hw; for mid messages tree could win if multicast path saturates. We need a microbenchmark sweep (node counts x msg sizes) to derive the real cross-over curve and bake into selector table.

liam: I'll run a quick sweep script on a 4/8/16 node topology. If we can reproduce p99 cliff we can quantify sticky_window length.

sophia: ack. I also observed kvcache eviction aligning with micro-batch boundaries — pushing some payloads into a different shard. I'll capture KV cache traces and upload.

marta: let's not revert code yet; apply sticky-mode flag on canary. If p99 improves -> ship hotfix that toggles sticky mode by default until we have sweep results.

liam: test plan: run 3 sweeps (4/8/16 nodes) across msg sizes [2KB,4KB,8KB,16KB,32KB,64KB,128KB], collect nccl_util, p99, handshake counts. Attach script:
```
for n in 4 8 16; do
  ./bench_tp_allreduce --nodes $n --sizes 2K,4K,8K,16K,32K,64K,128K --iter 500 --dump nccl_log_$n
done
```
I'll share results in this thread.

raj: if sweep pins crossover near ~24-40KB we should bias selector to prefer ring in that band to avoid flips. Also consider increasing batch aggregation in the runtime so KV merges reduce variance.

sophia: uploaded kvcache trace (small gz). Initial glance: lots of micro-second variance in merge timing when GC runs concurrently with micro-batch processing. That GC alignment seems to coincide with the worst p99 windows.

marta: ok next steps: (1) liam enable sticky_mode on canary, (2) liam run sweep, (3) sophia provide kvcache/gc trace annotated with bad windows, (4) raj prototype selector sticky-window and threshold smoothing. We'll reconvene when we have sweep results. If sticky_mode fixes it, we promote hotfix.

liam: enabling sticky_mode now. will post perf numbers within ~15m.

sophia: thanks. also created issue infra/runtime#7612 to track hotfix + benchmark POV.

marta: :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary restart completed. runtime-canary pod restarted in 00:01:45. Logs streaming to /logs/runtime-canary/1769009999

liam: quick update after sticky_mode=true on canary (short run): p99 for 16KB dropped from 18.2ms -> 6.9ms. ring/tree switchbacks dropped by ~95%. Looks promising.

sophia: great — thanks. Let's schedule the benchmark sweep and plan a short rollback of the selector change if needed.

marta: filing a short RFC for selector heuristics change and adding deterministic microbench in CI. We'll also add a metric: 'collective-routing-switchbacks/sec' to console.

sophia: closing loop — temporary mitigation in place, working on measurement. If anyone sees related incidents, drop logs here.
